headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill shifts the financial burden of grid infrastructure upgrades from residential ratepayers to large energy consumers like data centers, aiming to reduce household utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, environmental groups
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to Users
news_summary: New Virginia legislation requires data centers using 25 MW or more to pay for increased generating capacity, shifting energy costs to high-demand users. This aims to prevent these costs from being passed on to other customers.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This legislation requires data centers to publicly report their water usage, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact on local water resources.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental organizations, local communities, water conservation groups
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden)
news_headline: New Virginia Law Mandates Data Center Water Reporting
news_summary: A new state law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, with the data to be made publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide greater transparency and inform discourse around data center water consumption.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill empowers local governments to establish stricter zoning and noise regulations for data center developments, addressing community concerns about quality of life.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community associations, environmental advocates
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry, business associations
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Noise, Siting Assessments
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153 defines high-energy-use facilities, like data centers, as those requiring 100 megawatts or more, triggering special-exception requirements. This includes mandatory noise studies for facilities near homes and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
